newsitem.title: USA: VeriSign to unveil enhanced Digital ID features.
newsitem.headline: VeriSign to unveil enhanced Digital ID features.

text.p: VeriSign Inc executives said the company will Monday introduce new protection, secure e-mail and universal cryptographic log-in capabilities for its Digital ID certificates.

The digital certificates, which have been available to the public since August 1996, promote electronic commerce and communications by enabling users of the Internet and corporate intranets to initiate cryptographically secure transactions and communications.

Using a method known as public key encryption, VeriSign operates as an Internet certificate authority, a trusted third party that authenticates, issues and manages digital certificates for use on the Internet.
The certificates provide a hand shake which enables individuals to transact with commercial Web sites.

Among the new features are a protection program for consumers doing business on the Net, universal Web site log-in, a one-step registration process and round-the-clock directory access, revocation and replacement services.

The NetSure Protection plan, underwritten by the United States Fidelity & Guarantee Corp, offers consumers protection against economic loss due to impersonation, theft, corruption or loss of use of a Digital ID.
The service will be available in May and offers Class 1 coverage up to $1,000 for $9.95 a year and Class 2 coverage up to $25,000 a year for $19.95, it said.
A Class 3 $100,000 coverage will be available for Web sites starting in June, with consumer availability later this year.
VeriSign said it has issued over 750,000 Digital IDs since it opened its Digital ID center in August last year, while around 20,000 Web sites use the technology.
VeriSign is offering a free six-month evaluation Class 1 Digital ID through promotions with Netscape Communications Corp and Microsoft Corp.
Richard Yanowitch, a marketing executive at the company, said in an interview he expects this to increase into the millions in the coming year, with tens of thousands of Web sites using Digital IDs.
Other features include universal Web site log-in capability, which replaces user names and passwords with a cryptographically-secure two-way authentication.
The Digital IDs can now include basic registration data which can simplify registration at Web sites through use of the Digital ID.

Digital IDs support RSA Data Security's S/MIME protocol, which provides an interoperability standard for electronic mail security and is supported by Microsoft and Netscape as well as several Internet directory services.
Besides Microsoft and Netscape, those backing the new services include prominent Internet sites and companies such as The Motley Fool and Virtual Vineyards.
VeriSign said a Web site Digital ID Implementation kit is now available for $995 a year.

VeriSign is also targeting the corporate market and expects to eventually deploy hundreds of thousands of cards through branded company applications, such as a digital "wallet" that could store money.
Companies must make an initial investment of around $100,000 to set up the service, and then pay $1-$2 per certificate each year, with volume pricing discounts.
"We believe it's a huge market," Yanowitch said.
VeriSign was spun off from RSA Data Security before RSA's merger with Security Dynamics.

The private company's investors include those two companies, plus Microsoft, AT&T Corp, Cisco Systems, Comcast, Intuit, Reuters Holdings Plc, Softbank, Ameritech, First Data, GemPlus and Visa. ((sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau 415 846 5400))
